- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if price drops 5%+ from recent peak, forecast should not rise above 10% above prior low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (days 1–7); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.6) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true price as anchor for correction.
